questions.question: Which of the following is a yellowish green to green coloured gemstone often found in mafic and ultramafic igneous rocks such as basalt, gabbro, dunite, diabase and periodotite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Olivine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bornite:-**

 
 
• **It is a copper iron sulfide mineral that is commonly found in hydrothermal veins and contact metamorphic rocks. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tremolite:-**

 
 
• It is a calcium magnesium silicate mineral that belongs to the amphibole group and is commonly found in metamorphic rocks such as schist and marble.
 
 
 
• **Garnet:-**
 
 
• It is a group of minerals that come in a variety of colors and are commonly found in metamorphic and igneous rocks.
 
 
 
• **Olivine:-**
 
 
• It is a magnesium iron silicate mineral that is typically yellowish-green to green in color.
 
• Olivine is also known as peridot when it occurs as a gemstone.

questions.question: ______ are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deep sea plains**__.

__
 
• **Deep-sea plains are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Ocean Floor Division can be divided into various parts such as Continental Shelf, Continental Slope, Continental Rise or Foot, Deep Ocean basins, Abyssal plains or Deep Sea plain, Oceanic Trenches, Seamounts, and Guyots.
 
 
• **Deep-Sea Plain or Abyssal plain**

 
 
• These plains are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins.
 
• These are the flattest and smoothest regions of the world.
 
• It is an underwater plain on the deep ocean floor, usually found at depths between 3,000 and 6,000m.
 
• These plains are covered with fine-grained sediments like clay and silt.
 
• Lying generally between the foot of a continental rise and a mid-ocean ridge, abyssal plains cover more than 50% of the Earth’s surface.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic Deeps or Trenches**
 
 
• These areas are the deepest parts of the oceans.
 
• The trenches are relatively steep-sided, narrow basins.
 
• They are some 3-5 km deeper than the surrounding ocean floor.
 
• They occur at the bases of continental slopes and along island arcs and are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Continental Shelf**
 
 
• The continental shelf is the extended margin of each continent occupied by relatively shallow seas and gulfs.
 
• It is the shallowest part of the ocean showing an average gradient of 1° or even less.
 
• The shelf typically ends at a very steep slope, called the shelf break.
 
 
 
• **Continental Slope**
 
 
• The continental slope connects the continental shelf and the ocean basins.
 
• It begins where the bottom of the continental shelf sharply drops off into a steep slope.
 
• The gradient of the slope region varies between 2-5°.
 
• The depth of the slope region varies between 200 and 3,000 m.
 
• The slope boundary indicates the end of the continents.

questions.question: Which mineral salt is dissolved in a major amount in ocean water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium chloride.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium chloride**, also known as **table salt**, is a mineral salt that is dissolved in major amounts in **ocean water.**
 
• It is estimated that the ocean contains about **35 grams** of salt per liter of water, and about** 85% **of that salt is sodium chloride.
 
• **Calcium chloride and calcium sulfate** are also present in ocean water but in much **smaller amounts **compared to sodium chloride.
 
• Calcium carbonate is a mineral that is found in the** shells and skeletons** of many marine organisms, but it is** not dissolved **in ocean water as much as sodium chloride.
 
• The high concentration of sodium chloride in ocean water is one of the reasons why it is **not safe to drink** without proper treatment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium chloride** is a salt that is commonly used as a **de-icing agent** on roads and sidewalks, as well as in **food production and medical applications.**
 
• **Calcium sulphate**, also known as** gypsum**, is a mineral that is used in **construction, agriculture, and as a food additive.**
 
• **Calcium carbonate** is used in a variety of industries, including **construction, paper production, and as a dietary supplement.**
 
• It is important to note that while sodium chloride is the most **abundant mineral salt in ocean water,** there are also many other dissolved substances that contribute to the overall composition of seawater.

questions.question: El Nino is a climate pattern that describes the unusual warming of surface waters in which ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Pacific Ocean**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• El Niño is a climate pattern that describes the unusual warming of surface waters in the **eastern tropical Pacific Ocean**. 
 
• This warming event has significant impacts on weather patterns around the globe, affecting rainfall, temperature, and wind patterns.
 
• During an El Niño event, the trade winds, which typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean, weaken or reverse direction.
 
• This allows warm water to accumulate in the eastern Pacific, leading to changes in atmospheric pressure and circulation.
 
• The impacts of El Niño can be far-reaching, affecting weather patterns in regions as diverse as South America, Africa, and Southeast Asia.
 
• Some of the potential impacts of El Niño include:
 
 
• Increased rainfall: In some regions, such as the southern United States and parts of South America, El Niño can lead to increased rainfall and flooding.
 
• Drought: In other regions, such as Australia and Southeast Asia, El Niño can cause drought and reduced rainfall.
 
• Changes in ocean ecosystems: Warmer water temperatures can disrupt marine ecosystems, affecting fish populations and coral reefs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Arctic Ocean:**

 
 
• This is the smallest of the world's five oceans, located in the Northern Hemisphere. 
 
 
 
• **Indian Ocean:**
 
 
• This ocean is located between Africa, Asia, and Australia. 
 
 
 
• **Atlantic Ocean:**
 
 
• This ocean separates the Americas from Europe and Africa.

questions.question: In the higher latitudes (50° - 70°) of Northern hemisphere the spectacular Coniferous forests are found. These are also called as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Coniferous forests found in the higher latitudes (50° - 70°) of Northern Hemisphere are also called Boreal forests or Taiga.**
 
• They are characterized by a cold and harsh climate,** with long, cold winters and short, cool summers.**
 
• The dominant tree species in these forests are conifers such as **spruce, pine, and fir,** which are adapted to the harsh climate and poor soil conditions.
 
• The Boreal forest is an important ecosystem, providing habitat for a wide range of wildlife and playing a crucial role in global carbon cycling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Veld -**

 
 
• Veld is a term used to describe open grassland areas found in** Southern Africa,** especially in **South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, and Namibia.**
 
• These regions are characterized by a **semi-arid to arid climate with dry, hot summers and cool, dry winters.**
 
• The vegetation in the veld varies from** grassland **to** savanna** with scattered **trees and shrubs.**
 
• The grasses in the veld are adapted to withstand drought and fire, and are often grazed by large herbivores such as antelopes and zebras.
 
• The veld is an important ecosystem for biodiversity, supporting a wide range of animal and plant species, including many endemic and threatened species.
 
• It is also used for livestock grazing and agriculture, making it an important economic resource for the region.
 
 
 
• **Tundra -**
 
 
• Tundra is a type of biome characterized by its **low temperatures, short growing season, and lack of trees.**
 
• It is found in the Arctic and Alpine regions, where the ground is frozen for much of the year (permafrost) and the climate is **harsh and cold.**
 
• The tundra is covered in low-lying vegetation, including mosses, lichens, grasses, and small shrubs, and is home to a variety of animal species such as **caribou, musk oxen, Arctic foxes, and polar bears.**
 
• Due to its extreme environment, the tundra is a fragile ecosystem that is particularly vulnerable to human activities such as **oil and gas exploration, mining, and climate change.**
 
• It is also an important carbon sink, helping to regulate the Earth's climate by storing large amounts of carbon in its** frozen soil.**
 
 
 
• **​The** **Llanos** -
 
 
• The Llanos, also known as Los Llanos, is a vast tropical grassland plain located in South America, primarily in Venezuela and Colombia.
 
• The region is characterized by its flat terrain, with grassy plains that are often flooded during the rainy season and dry and dusty during the dry season.
 
• The Llanos is home to a diverse array of wildlife, including capybaras, anacondas, jaguars, giant anteaters, and many species of birds.
 
• The grasslands also support large numbers of domesticated animals, such as cattle and horses, and are an important agricultural region for both countries.
 
• The Llanos is also a popular destination for ecotourism, with visitors coming to observe wildlife and experience the traditional cowboy culture of the region.

questions.question: The _________ is responsible for Earth's magnetic field.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The interior of the earth is divided into three parts namely **Crust, Mantle, and Core.**
 
• **The core **is the innermost layer of the earth.
 
• The radius of the innermost layer(core) is about **3500 km.**
 
• The core is made up of material constituted by **nickel and iron.**
 
• The temperature and pressure of the central core are very high.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The core is further subdivided into two layers called the **outer core and inner core.**
 
• The outer core of the earth is in a liquid state.
 
• The inner core is in solid-state
 
• The outer core is responsible for the **earth's magnetic field.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **crust** is the outermost of the earth.

 
 
• It is brittle in nature.
 
• it the thinnest layer of Earth.
 
• The thickness of the crust varies under the oceanic and continental areas.
 
 
 
• **The mantle** is the second layer in the interior of the earth.
 
 
• The mantle extends from Moho’s discontinuity to a depth of 2,900 km.
 
• The upper portion of the mantle is called the asthenosphere.

questions.question: What is the other name of black cotton soil found in Maharashtra?

questions.question: _______ are built up by the liquid and solid rock erupting from the earth’s interior.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volcanoes**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A volcano is a conical hill or mountain built around a vent that connects to reservoirs of molten rock beneath the Earth's surface**__.

 __
 
• Volcanoes are formed from liquid and solid rock emanating from the interior of the Earth.
 
• A hole or vent from which molten rock and associated gases escape is also called a volcano.
 
• Volcanoes are mountains, but they are not like other mountains, because they do not result from folding and crumpling, or uplift and erosion.
 
• Volcanoes are formed by the accumulation of explosive materials such as lava and bombs.
 
• Volcanoes occur most often on Earth when tectonic plates are separating or convergent, and most of them are found underwater.
 
• Basalt, a form of lava that is typically liquid when erupted, forms most volcanoes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fault-block mountains **are formed by the movement of large crustal blocks, which are formed when stressing forces pull the crust apart.
 
• **Circum-erosional or relict or residual mountains** (Aravallis in India, Urals in Russia) are remnants of older fold mountains that have resulted from denudation. Residual mountains may also develop from plateaus that have been divided by rivers into hills and valleys.
 
• A **plateau **is a flat, elevated landform that rises sharply from the surrounding area on at least one side. Plateaus occur on every continent and occupy one-third of the Earth's landmass. They are one of the four major landforms along with mountains, plains and hills.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is **NOT **correct about alluvial soil?

options.text: Old alluvial is called ‘bangar’ and new alluvial is called ‘khadar’.
Deltas of Mahanadi, the Godavari and the Krishna are made from alluvial soil
Northern plains are made of alluvial soil
In the Himalayan region we find alluvial soil.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__In the Himalayan region we find alluvial soil.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil is not found In the Himalayan region.**
 
• **Alluvial soils:**
 
 
• These soils are called** transported soil** because although they are formed near the water bodies, these soils get transported from their origin to several other places by various natural agents, especially by gravity.
 
• The alluvial soil is made up of particles like **silt, sand, and clay and has an adequate amount of phosphoric acid, potash, and lime.**
 
• It is of two types:
 
 
• The older alluvial soil is known as **Bhangar.**
 
• The newer alluvial soil is known as** Khadar.**
 
 
 
• The alluvial soil covers a total of** 40%** of the land.
 
• These soils are found in the **northern plains beginning from Punjab to West Bengal and Assam.**
 
• It is also** found in deltas of rivers like Krishna, Godavari, Kaveri, and Mahanadi in peninsular India.**
 
• The** main crops **cultivated are wheat, rice, maize, sugarcane, pulses, and oilseeds.

questions.question: At places the groundwater is stored between layers of hard rock below the water table. This is known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **an aquifer**

__
 
• An aquifer is an underground layer of porous rocks or permeable rocks that store and retain groundwater levels in the soil.
 
• The underground aquifer is built with all types of porous or permeable rock materials, such as sand, gravel, or silt, making it a suitable water absorber.
 
• The rainwater enters the aquifer through the soil and becomes a part of the groundwater.
 
• The groundwater from the aquifers then resurfaces from springs and wells.
 
• We can also extract the aquifer water with the help of a water well.
 
• The study of groundwater, aquifer, and their property is known as hydrogeology.

questions.question: In the context of mapping climate data, what term refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isoneph:-**

 
 
• **It refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud. **
 
• It is a type of isoline, which is a line that connects points of equal value.
 
• **Other common isolines include contour lines (elevation), isobars (atmospheric pressure), and isotherms (temperature).**
 
• Isonephs are used by meteorologists and climatologists to visualize the distribution of cloud cover over a region.
 
• **They can be used to identify areas of high and low cloud cover, as well as to track the movement of clouds over time.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isohels:-**

 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal sunshine duration.
 
 
 
• **Isocheims:-**
 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal temperature.
 
 
 
• **Isochalaz:-**
 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal hail size.

questions.question: What type of rocks was once igneous or sedimentary, but have metamorphosed as a result of intense heat and/or pressure within the Earth's crust?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quartzite.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__****Quartzite**

__
 
• **Quartzite is a non-foliated metamorphic rock.**
 
• It is composed almost entirely of **quartz.**
 
• **It forms when a quartz-rich sandstone is altered by the heat, pressure, and chemical activity of metamorphism.**
 
• They were once igneous or sedimentary.
 
• They have metamorphosed as a result of intense heat and/or pressure within the Earth's crust.
 
• The quartz content of quartzite gives it a hardness of about seven on the Mohs Hardness Scale.
 
• **Most quartzite forms during mountain-building events **at convergent plate boundaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Granite**

 
• **Granite is an example of igneous rock.**
 
• Due to the large presence of silica in its composition, **granite is highly resistant to decay.**
 
• Granite is an** easily quarried stone.**
 
• This is due to the** presence of a mural joint. **

**Sandstone**

 
• **Sandstone is a sedimentary rock.**
 
• It is **composed of sand-size grains rock fragments, minerals, and organic material.**
 
• Sand-size **particles range in size from 1/16 millimetres to 2 millimetres in diameter.**

**Basalt**

 
• **Basalt is the most common rock on Earth’s surface.**
 
• Specimens are** black in colour** and weather to **dark green or brown.**
 
• Basalt is** rich in iron and magnesium.**
 
• It is **composed of olivine, pyroxene, and plagioclase.**
 
• Most specimens are **compact, fine-grained, and glassy.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding laterite soil?

options.text: Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala are more suitable for crops like cashew nut.
They are generally rich in humus.
This soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee.
The laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **They are generally rich in humus**: This statement is NOT correct.
 
• **Laterite soils are generally low in fertility and organic matter, including humus.**
 
• They are often leached of essential nutrients due to heavy rainfall and have a low capacity to retain organic matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala** **are more suitable for crops like cashew nut: **Red laterite soils found in these regions have good drainage properties and are rich in iron and aluminum oxides.

 
 
• These soil characteristics make them suitable for crops like **cashew nut**, which thrive in well-drained soils.
 
 
 
• **This soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee:** Laterite soils are suitable for growing tea and coffee.
 
 
• These crops require well-drained soils with good water-holding capacity, and the characteristics of laterite soils, such as their ability to retain moisture, make them conducive to tea and coffee cultivation.
 
 
 
• **The laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall: **Laterite soils are primarily found in tropical and subtropical regions with high temperatures and heavy rainfall.
 
 
• The intense weathering and leaching processes that occur in these regions contribute to the formation of laterite soils.
